sections.title: Methods of persuasion
sections.content:
Vocabulary for how people convince others:
• persuade — convince someone to do something. She persuaded him to apply for the scholarship.
• manipulate — influence someone unfairly. He tried to manipulate the situation in his favour.
• negotiate — discuss terms to reach agreement. The unions negotiated a better pay deal.
• incentive — something that motivates action. Tax cuts serve as an incentive for investment.
• endorsement — public approval or support. Celebrity endorsement can significantly boost product sales.

sections.title: Being influenced
sections.content:
How people are affected by influence:
• gullible — easily deceived. Don't be so gullible — not everything online is true.
• sway — influence opinion. The emotional speech swayed public opinion.
• peer pressure — influence from people your age. Teenagers often give in to peer pressure.
• coerce — force someone to act. Nobody should be coerced into making a decision.
• charisma — compelling charm that inspires. Great leaders often have natural charisma.

exercises.question: Convincing someone through unfair or dishonest means is:
exercises.explanation: Manipulate means to control or influence someone cleverly or unscrupulously.

exercises.question: A person easily tricked or deceived is:
exercises.explanation: Gullible means easily persuaded to believe something; naive.

exercises.question: A motivation that encourages people to act is an:
exercises.explanation: An incentive is something that motivates or encourages someone to do something.

exercises.question: Forcing someone to do something against their will is to:
exercises.explanation: Coerce means to persuade someone by using force or threats.

exercises.question: Public support from a famous person is an:
exercises.hint: A celebrity says they like a product.
exercises.explanation: An endorsement is a public declaration of approval or support.

exercises.question: The compelling charm that inspires devotion in others is:
exercises.explanation: Charisma is compelling attractiveness or charm that can inspire devotion.

exercises.question: Influence from friends or people your own age is:
exercises.explanation: Peer pressure is influence from members of one's own age group.

exercises.question: To influence someone's opinion or feelings is to:
exercises.explanation: Sway means to influence the opinions or actions of someone.
